name: Joomla Component Builder
summary: A compiler-oriented development platform for generating native Joomla components, plugins, modules, and supporting code across multiple Joomla generations.
value: JCB turns architecture, schemas, reusable code, and extension metadata into repeatable builds. Its significance is not a single component: it is the maintained system that produces and evolves families of systems.
role: Principal architect and long-term steward since 2014/15; public canonical Git history from 2016.
architecture: Version-aware compilation separates shared intent from Joomla-generation-specific output.
Structured definitions drive extension generation instead of relying on one-off manual assembly.
Reusable Powers and Super Powers give generated systems stable references to shared implementation units.
Build, package, import/export, and repository-sync concerns are designed as parts of one lifecycle.
interfaces: Structured component, field, view, and extension definitions
Generated PHP, JavaScript, XML, SQL, and configuration assets
decisions: Encode repeatable architecture in generators while retaining version-specific output boundaries.
Treat backwards compatibility, upgrade paths, and long-term maintenance as first-class design constraints.
Separate reusable implementation units from any one generated extension.
quality: Versioned releases and public change history
Generated output inspection and package validation
Extensive public documentation and contributor-facing material

name: GetBible v3 publication pipeline
summary: A Python 3.12 build system that converts SWORD module output into a deterministic, validated, checksummed static API.
value: The pipeline creates a controlled publication boundary between native source extraction and downstream consumers. It validates framing and contracts, produces deterministic artifacts, and refuses publication when integrity conditions fail.
architecture: Native SWORD extraction is consumed through a line-oriented NDJSON contract.
Transformation stages normalize content into versioned static API artifacts.
Validation checks framing, schemas, identifiers, checksums, and publication expectations.
Build output is deterministic so releases can be compared, reproduced, and audited.
interfaces: Static API v3 files and indexes
decisions: Use a streaming contract to keep the native and Python responsibilities independently testable.
Fail closed: malformed or incomplete inputs do not become public artifacts.
Preserve stable identifiers and editorial semantics across transformation.

name: GetBibleSWORD
summary: A native C++20 extraction engine for CrossWire SWORD modules with a CLI, stable C ABI, deterministic NDJSON output, and cross-architecture releases.
value: The engine isolates native library concerns behind explicit machine interfaces, allowing build pipelines and other consumers to use SWORD data without inheriting its implementation complexity.
architecture: A native core reads SWORD modules and emits a versioned NDJSON protocol.
The command-line interface supports batch and pipeline operation.
A stable C ABI exposes library functionality to other runtimes without a C++ ABI dependency.
Release workflows target x86_64 and arm64.
decisions: Use C++ for direct SWORD integration and a C ABI for broad language interoperability.
Keep output deterministic and line-oriented for validation, streaming, and failure isolation.
Treat the protocol as a contract rather than an incidental serialization detail.

name: Joomla MCP
summary: A TypeScript MCP server that maps a source-catalogued Joomla Web Services surface into structured tools with guarded write operations.
value: The project connects agent reasoning to a real application platform while keeping tool contracts, write permissions, audit concerns, and transport boundaries explicit.
architecture: Route templates are catalogued from source and projected into MCP tools.
Read and write concerns are separated, with writes placed behind explicit guards.
Transport supports stdio and HTTP integration modes.
Companion and API layers isolate Joomla-specific behavior from protocol concerns.
decisions: Catalogue routes from source instead of relying on an unverified manual list.
Make mutating operations visibly different and explicitly controlled.
Report validation status accurately; a catalogued route is not automatically a production-certified route.
quality: Public validation status and known limits

name: OpenCode Platform
summary: A source-controlled family of Ubuntu 24.04 Incus VM images for PHP, Python, C++, TypeScript, and combined engineering work.
value: The platform makes language environments, agent tooling, and operational boundaries reproducible while keeping credentials and network access outside the image source.
architecture: Layered base, language-specific, and full images keep shared concerns centralized.
Source control is the definition of the environment rather than a manually configured machine.
Joomla MCP integration is available in relevant images without embedding deployment secrets.
Credential and network boundaries are documented as external operational concerns.
decisions: Prefer full virtual-machine isolation where development tasks need system-level tools.
Keep secrets out of images and source-controlled configuration.
Use a compositional image family instead of duplicating every toolchain.

name: Joomla Docker
summary: Official Joomla container image work covering repeatable builds, image variants, multi-architecture publication, and upstream delivery constraints.
value: This work demonstrates framework knowledge at the delivery boundary: the application, runtime, operating image, release process, and official-images requirements must agree.
architecture: Image variants express supported runtime and web-server combinations.
Build definitions track Joomla releases and upstream base images.
Official-images integration adds review and publication constraints beyond a private image build.
decisions: Keep images reproducible and understandable from source.
Support architecture and runtime variants without hiding their differences.
Coordinate application releases with upstream container publication requirements.

name: JCB Super Powers
summary: A central registry of reusable, namespaced PHP classes, interfaces, traits, and abstractions referenced through stable identifiers and injected through JCB.
value: The registry separates reusable architecture from individual generated systems and gives code units a stable identity across projects and build contexts.
architecture: Reusable implementation units are stored independently from consuming extensions.
Stable identifiers allow generators to resolve and inject the required units.
Namespacing and explicit dependencies reduce accidental coupling.
decisions: Make reuse explicit and source-controlled instead of copying code between extensions.
Use stable references so generated projects can evolve independently of registry layout.

name: GetBible Flutter
summary: A typed, local-data-first Flutter reader designed for Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux targets.
value: The project extends the publication architecture into a private, cross-platform client with a typed domain model and local database boundary.
architecture: Typed domain and data layers isolate application behavior from storage and presentation.
Drift and SQLite provide local persistence without requiring an account-based runtime service.
Platform targets share application logic while retaining target-specific packaging.
decisions: Prefer local data and privacy-preserving operation.
Keep development status explicit rather than implying completed store distribution.

name: Joomla project service
summary: A sustained official volunteer record spanning production, infrastructure, strategy, directory, language, testing, mentoring, and leadership responsibilities.
value: The record demonstrates contribution beyond code: maintaining shared systems, coordinating work, reviewing changes, supporting contributors, and participating in project direction.
role: Volunteer, maintainer, mentor, team leader, and strategy contributor across multiple teams.
architecture: Production and infrastructure responsibilities connect framework decisions to operational reality.
Strategy and working-group service connects implementation detail to project-wide direction.
Testing, mentoring, and directory work require cross-team communication and sustained maintenance.
decisions: Treat community systems and documentation as maintained engineering products.
Contribute across code, operations, review, coordination, and teaching.

name: Long-running professional systems
summary: A portfolio of institutional, commercial, workflow, information, and operational systems maintained across long working relationships.
value: The record shows architecture under non-demo conditions: changing requirements, production continuity, hosting, security, data stewardship, support, and maintenance.
role: Independent architect, developer, operator, and technical lead through Vast Development Method.
architecture: Information and workflow systems are designed around the organization’s operating model.
Delivery includes hosting, maintenance, support, recovery, and change management.
Long-lived systems require migration and compatibility decisions as frameworks and infrastructure evolve.
interfaces: Hosting, source control, and secrets infrastructure
decisions: Avoid publishing private client implementation details beyond the supplied professional record.
Represent continuing work by verified relationship and scope, not invented outcomes or metrics.
